links: The thorax houses a heart roughly twice the mass allometry predicts, paired with massive alveolar surface area and high capillary density that shrink oxygen diffusion distance.
High myoglobin stores buffer oxygen in muscle, letting the animal hold a VO₂ max several times that of a similar mammal without accumulating lactate.
On the open grasslands where cover is absent, endurance beats sprint: a larger engine sustains minutes of flight rather than seconds of acceleration.
This matches the F29 template for open-habitat cursorial survival, though rival hypotheses cite leg length or thermoregulation.

skill.effect: The pronghorn maintains a steady, swift pace across open terrain, moving easily over rough ground and outlasting any chasers who rely on short bursts of speed.

chains.weakness: it is built to run past obstacles, not over them: it will not jump a fence and instead crawls underneath, so a fenceline corners it
observe: a chase that lasts minutes while the predator gives up in seconds
a barrel chest on legs that look too thin for it
hair snagged under the bottom wire of a fence, never over the top

journal.en: It runs from a predator that has been extinct for ten thousand years.

analogues.organism: Antilocapra americana — elite aerobic capacity and sustained running (Lindstedt et al.); selection context: open plains + historic cursorial predation (Byers 'ghosts of predators past')
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Dense winter pelage with medullated guard hairs
links: Thick guard hairs pack densely to trap a still-air boundary layer against the skin, where thermal resistance R scales with thickness d and low conductivity k.
On the exposed continental interior, wind strips that boundary layer, so survival depends on maintaining R against convective heat loss rather than relying on hollow lumens.
F4’s axial tilt drives the annual solar swing, while inferred continental wind patterns demand a coat that can be shed when the sun returns.
The moult leaves patchy bare skin in spring, turning winter insulation into a heat trap before the new undercoat fully forms.

skill.effect: no cold penalty down to -45 °C wind chill and full stamina regeneration while bedded in snow; a distinct blue-ice Overheat meter fills twice as fast under summer sun, forcing shade or water before it tops out

chains.weakness: between the spring moult and the new coat the fur is patchy, bare skin burns and the Overheat meter runs hot: corner it in open sun at midday, or pen it behind a fence it will not jump, and the winter-proof coat becomes a summer trap
observe: a shed guard hair snapped in two showing a fibrous core rather than a hollow tube
it stands rump to the wind while everything else faces away
in late spring the coat lifts in patchy tufts with pink bare skin showing

journal.en: A desert coat worn in a blizzard, and a blizzard coat worn in the sun.

plausibility.summary: Tie -45 °C wind-chill survival to calm-to-moderate wind unless 'bedded in snow' explicitly adds microclimate; pronghorn still suffer extreme exposure during blizzards.
fixes: Tie -45 °C wind-chill survival to calm-to-moderate wind unless 'bedded in snow' explicitly adds microclimate; pronghorn still suffer extreme exposure during blizzards.

chains.trait: Laterally placed orbits with wide interorbital spacing
links: The orbits sit high and far back on the skull, maximizing horizontal field of view to roughly 320° while compressing binocular overlap to a narrow wedge of about 32°.
This optical geometry sacrifices stereoscopic depth perception for early motion detection at the visual periphery.
On the treeless plains of F29, cover is absent, so spotting a moving stalker long before shape resolution dictates survival.
The trade-off leaves a blind sector directly behind and poor close-range depth judgment, forcing the animal to rely on herd vigilance and early flight.

skill.effect: The pronghorn's wide-set eyes scan the horizon, spotting hidden creatures from afar and alerting the group before danger strikes. Its keen sight weakens in thick vegetation, but it still catches movement early.

chains.weakness: the eyes trade binocular overlap for width: it is poor at judging close range and blind in a wedge directly behind, so a stalker that gets inside 40 m from downwind is invisible to it
observe: eyes on the flanks of the head with almost no forward overlap
a head that lifts from grazing every few seconds, always the same direction
a sharp snort given at something you cannot see yet

journal.en: It watches the horizon so hard it forgets to watch its feet.

plausibility.summary: 800 m 'concealed ambusher' is generous for cryptic stalker in tall grass; reserve 800 m for obvious motion on open plain; scrub halve detection. Binocular overlap ~32° (ungulate typ.) supports close-range depth weakness.

relations.note: Both track the same open-habitat pressure. Cenozoic cooling expanded grasslands, selecting for endurance over burst speed. Humans trade agility for striding and sweating; pronghorn trade maneuverability for massive cardio and panoramic vision. Playable: players can use human heat-dissipation to outlast pronghorn in summer, or follow pronghorn migration routes to find water.

Grassland mutualism. Ravens follow herds to eat ticks and disturbed insects; pronghorn gain early warning against terrestrial predators. Playable: befriending ravens grants a 'sentinel' alert when pronghorn herds shift direction, revealing hidden water or predators.

Historical hunting pressure. Humans tracked pronghorn across Pleistocene-Holocene steppe corridors, using endurance and fire to exhaust them; pronghorn rely on speed and terrain to escape. Playable: players can use human pursuit tactics to corner pronghorn, or preserve migration routes to unlock stamina bonuses.
